description: Document the end-state architecture of Helping Hands in the repo's main docs (README or an architecture doc) so future work aligns to it. The end result is an agentic harness that talks to a world action model. Two layers: (1) the world action model — trained on our gripper's data, it understands the world and how to physically interact with it (low-level manipulation); (2) above it, an LLM agent harness that runs tool calls to get things done in the real world, with the world action model exposed to it as the thing that executes actions.

results.identified_issue: Repo had no README; architecture notes were scattered across plans/ (world_action_model.md, molmoact2*.md, agent_led_research.md). Put the end state in a new root README.md as the single main doc rather than another plans/ file, so it's the first thing any agent reads. Framed current MolmoAct2/FLUX checkpoints as layer-1 placeholders. Named robot_eval/protocol.py's POST /act (instruction + state + stereo images -> action chunk) as today's layer 1<->2 contract, since it already takes a plain-language instruction. Tool names act()/look()/stop() are illustrative, not an implemented API. Agent harness is marked 'not built yet'. Did not edit any plans/ docs.
results.summary: Added a root README that documents the end-state architecture: an LLM agent harness on top of a world action model trained on our gripper's data.
results.detailed_description:
The repo had no README, so I added one at the root. It describes the two layers. Layer 1 is the world action model, trained on our gripper's data, which turns cameras plus a short instruction into actions. Layer 2 is the LLM agent harness, which plans and makes tool calls, with the world action model exposed to it as the tool that carries out physical actions.

It names the boundary between them: a tool call where an instruction goes in and a physical action comes out. Today that's the POST /act contract in robot_eval/protocol.py. The README also says that retrying belongs to the agent, not the policy, and that MolmoAct2 and FLUX are stand-ins until we have our own model. A table at the end assigns each part of the repo to a layer. The agent harness is listed as "not built yet."

Tool names like act() and look() are only examples, not a real API. Please read it and tell me whether anything should be framed differently.

summary: Helping Hands' main docs don't describe its end-state architecture: an LLM agent harness running tool calls above a gripper-trained world action model. Document those two layers, with the world action model exposed as the executor of low-level physical manipulation, so future work aligns.
